claims.economy: The Ijaw people live by fishing supplemented by farming and trading; smoke-dried fish, timber, palm oil and palm kernels are processed for export.
claims.food: Ijaw foods include fried or roasted fish and plantain, fish fried in palm oil and served with fried plantains, and Opuru-fulou, a prawn soup prepared mainly with prawn, ogbono, dried fish, crayfish, onions, pepper and red palm oil.
claims.masks: Ijaw water-spirit celebrations centre on masquerades in which men wearing elaborate outfits and carved masks dance to drums.
